data.name: Labanya
data.long_meaning: Labanya is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Labh' meaning 'to obtain'. The name Labanya signifies the goddess of gratitude and prosperity. It is believed that this name bestows blessings of abundance and contentment upon the bearer. In Hindu mythology, Labanya is the goddess of wealth and abundance. She is often depicted holding a lotus or a bowl of rice, symbolizing prosperity and nourishment.

historical_references.reference: Labanyas are mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, as the wives of the five Pandava brothers. They are also referred to as the 'Kaikeyis' of the Pandavas, as they were given to the brothers by their mother Kunti.

Another reference to Labanya is in the Bengali literature, where Labanya is a character in the Bengali classic 'Chandi Ondhokar' written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1884. In this work, Labanya is a courtesan who plays a significant role in the plot.
